title: sharded-multipart-embed-uploader-with-progress-hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers ingesting large document collections for embeddings (millions of documents) hit a mix of problems: upload timeouts, duplicated work on retry, high memory spikes when the service tries to batch entire uploads, and poor visibility into progress. This ticket designs and implements a sharded multipart upload + async-job flow for bulk embedding ingestion with deterministic idempotency behavior and progress hooks for Console.

Goal: Provide an ingestion path that supports (1) streaming multipart uploads for large files and many small files, (2) automatic sharding and backpressure-aware batching on the server to bound memory, (3) async job lifecycle + retryable idempotency keys so retries are safe and deduplicated, and (4) progress callbacks (webhooks) and Console hooks to show per-job, per-shard progress. The API should preserve low-latency single-document embed calls and improve reranking latency by enabling early partial results and caching intermediate embeddings.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/embeddings/bulk with multipart/form-data or ndjson accepts an optional idempotency-key and returns job_id for async processing when payload > 10MB
Resumability: Large uploads can be uploaded in shards; server accepts shard range and a manifest and can resume from last acknowledged shard
Idempotency: Re-sending same idempotency-key within 7 days does not create duplicate jobs; server provides deterministic job outcome or job_id return
Backpressure/batching: Server batches tokens/requests to keep peak GPU memory bounded; no OOM observed in load test up to 2M docs/day per cluster
Progress hooks: Webhook callbacks (job.started, shard.progress, job.completed, job.failed) firing with consistent aggregate percent completion; Console shows progress bar per job
Retries: Exactly-once or at-most-once semantics for document embedding persistence depending on customer choice; default deduplicate-on-id field
Performance: Small-file streaming mode measured at median end-to-end ingest latency < 120ms per 1k docs in streaming mode; large-batch async throughput achieves target tokens/sec from perf plan
Rerank integration: Reranker can accept partial embedding sets (streaming update) and produce initial ranked results with graceful degradation until full job completes
Monitoring: Job metrics (jobs_started, jobs_completed, jobs_failed, shards_uploaded, idempotency_conflicts) emitted to metrics backend and dashboards created
Tests: Unit and integration tests for manifest parsing, idempotency conflict resolution, shard resume, webhook retries, and end-to-end ingestion on staging
tasks: Write API spec and OpenAPI definitions for bulk endpoint and job status endpoints
Design shard manifest format and resumable upload semantics (byte-range + shard IDs + checksums)
Implement server-side shard coordinator that creates deterministic job_id from idempotency-key and manifest fingerprint
Implement upload worker that converts shards into bounded batches and writes to embedding pipeline with backpressure
Add job store schema and migration for job metadata, shard state, and idempotency keys
Wire webhook progress hooks and Console subscription for job updates
Add retry semantics: client-visible retry headers and server-side dedupe logic
Create automated load tests to validate throughput and memory profiles
Add integration tests for resume, conflict, and duplicate submission behavior
Create Console UX mock and implement small progress UI for jobs
notes: Design trade-offs: choose deterministic job_id derivation from (idempotency-key || manifest_hash). Using manifest_hash only would break client-friendly retries where payload is modified; prefer idempotency-key as primary with manifest fallback.
Dedup strategy: default to dedupe-on-(client_document_id) if provided, otherwise dedupe by SHA256 of document payload. Provide customer knob to control at-most-once vs at-least-once semantics.
Shard sizing: default 10k documents / shard or ~50MB per shard; auto-adjust based on token estimates and observed sequence length distributions to avoid oversized KV caches.
Rerank interaction: producer publishes partial embedding sets to ephemeral topic; reranker can subscribe and emit interim ranked results into a materialized view used by Console and API endpoints.
Security: ensure idempotency-key is treated as an opaque token and logged only hashed; webhook payloads signed with HMAC and replay-protected
S3-like staging: use existing object storage with lifecycle TTL for temporary shards (48h), expunge after job completion or cancellation

Related: see ENG-17602 for streaming uploader lessons and ENG-16234 for async batch API patterns. This ticket implements a different surface (multipart sharding + progress hooks) and a stricter idempotency model.
